sanskrit: kathāṃ vetsi mune divyāṃ manuṣyoragarakṣasām etad icchāmy ahaṃ śrotuṃ tattvena kathitaṃ dvija
english: You know the divine story, O sage, of humans, serpents, and demons. I wish to hear it narrated in truth, O twice-born one.

sanskrit: kuvalāśva iti khyāta ikṣvākur aparājitaḥ kathaṃ nāma viparyāsād dhundhumāratvam āgataḥ
english: The unconquered Ikṣvāku known as Kuvalāśva — how did he come to be called Dhundhumāra through that strange reversal of name?

sanskrit: etad icchāmi tattvena jñātuṃ bhārgavasattama viparyastaṃ yathā nāma kuvalāśvasya dhīmataḥ
english: I wish to know this in truth, O best of the Bhārgava line — how the name of the wise Kuvalāśva became thus reversed.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca hanta te kathayiṣyāmi śṛṇu rājan yudhiṣṭhira dharmiṣṭham idam ākhyānaṃ dhundhumārasya tac chṛṇu
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Very well, I shall tell you. Listen, O king Yudhiṣṭhira — hear this most righteous tale of Dhundhumāra.

sanskrit: yathā sa rājā ikṣvākuḥ kuvalāśvo mahīpatiḥ dhundhumāratvam agamat tac chṛṇuṣva mahīpate
english: How that Ikṣvāku king, Kuvalāśva, lord of the earth, came to be called Dhundhumāra — hear that, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: maharṣir viśrutas tāta uttaṅka iti bhārata marudhanvasu ramyeṣu āśramas tasya kaurava
english: There was a great sage of fame, O dear one, called Uttaṅka, O Bhārata — his hermitage stood in the pleasant sandy desert wastes, O Kaurava.

sanskrit: uttaṅkas tu mahārāja tapo 'tapyat suduścaram ārirādhayiṣur viṣṇuṃ bahūn varṣagaṇān vibho
english: Uttaṅka, O great king, practiced severe and arduous austerities for many groups of years, O lord, desiring to propitiate Viṣṇu.

sanskrit: tasya prītaḥ sa bhagavān sākṣād darśanam eyivān dṛṣṭvaiva carṣiḥ prahvas taṃ tuṣṭāva vividhaiḥ stavaiḥ
english: Pleased with him, the blessed Lord came to grant him a vision in person. And the sage, bowing as soon as he saw him, praised him with various hymns.

sanskrit: tvayā deva prajāḥ sarvāḥ sadevāsuramānavāḥ sthāvarāṇi ca bhūtāni jaṅgamāni tathaiva ca brahma vedāś ca vedyaṃ ca tvayā sṛṣṭaṃ mahādyute
english: By you, O god, all creatures together with gods, asuras, and humans, stationary and moving beings likewise, Brahmā, the Vedas, and all that is knowable — all have been created, O greatly radiant one.

sanskrit: śiras te gaganaṃ deva netre śaśidivākarau niḥśvāsaḥ pavanaś cāpi tejo 'gniś ca tavācyuta bāhavas te diśaḥ sarvāḥ kukṣiś cāpi mahārṇavaḥ
english: Your head is the sky, O god; your two eyes are the moon and sun; your breath is the wind; your splendor is fire, O Acyuta; your arms are all the directions; your belly is the great ocean.

sanskrit: ūrū te parvatā deva khaṃ nābhir madhusūdana pādau te pṛthivī devī romāṇy oṣadhayas tathā
english: Your thighs are the mountains, O god; the ether is your navel, O Madhusūdana; your feet are the divine earth; your body hair is the herbs and plants.

sanskrit: indrasomāgnivaruṇā devāsuramahoragāḥ prahvās tvām upatiṣṭhanti stuvanto vividhaiḥ stavaiḥ
english: Indra, Soma, Agni, Varuṇa — gods, asuras, and great serpents — bowing, attend upon you, praising you with various hymns.

sanskrit: tvayā vyāptāni sarvāṇi bhūtāni bhuvaneśvara yoginaḥ sumahāvīryāḥ stuvanti tvāṃ maharṣayaḥ
english: All beings are pervaded by you, O lord of the worlds. Great sages with mighty spiritual power, the yogins, praise you.

sanskrit: tvayi tuṣṭe jagat svasthaṃ tvayi kruddhe mahad bhayam bhayānām apanetāsi tvam ekaḥ puruṣottama
english: When you are pleased the world is well; when you are wrathful there is great fear. You alone are the remover of all fears, O supreme Person.

sanskrit: devānāṃ mānuṣāṇāṃ ca sarvabhūtasukhāvahaḥ tribhir vikramaṇair deva trayo lokās tvayāhṛtāḥ asurāṇāṃ samṛddhānāṃ vināśaś ca tvayā kṛtaḥ
english: You bring happiness to gods, humans, and all beings. With three strides, O god, you reclaimed the three worlds; and by you the destruction of the prosperous asuras was accomplished.

sanskrit: tava vikramaṇair devā nirvāṇam agaman param parābhavaṃ ca daityendrās tvayi kruddhe mahādyute
english: Through your strides the gods attained supreme liberation, and the lords of the Daityas met their defeat when you were wrathful, O greatly radiant one.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi kartā vikartā ca bhūtānām iha sarvaśaḥ ārādhayitvā tvāṃ devāḥ sukham edhanti sarvaśaḥ
english: You indeed are the creator and destroyer of all beings here in every way. Having propitiated you, the gods prosper in happiness on every side.

sanskrit: evaṃ stuto hṛṣīkeśa uttaṅkena mahātmanā uttaṅkam abravīd viṣṇuḥ prītas te 'haṃ varaṃ vṛṇu
english: Thus praised, O Hrishikesha, by the great-souled Uttaṅka, Viṣṇu said to Uttaṅka: "I am pleased — choose a boon."

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca paryāpto me varo hy eṣa yad ahaṃ dṛṣṭavān harim puruṣaṃ śāśvataṃ divyaṃ sraṣṭāraṃ jagataḥ prabhum
english: Uttaṅka said: This itself is boon enough for me, that I have seen Hari — the eternal, divine Person, the creator and lord of the universe.

sanskrit: viṣṇur uvāca prītas te 'ham alaulyena bhaktyā ca dvijasattama avaśyaṃ hi tvayā brahman matto grāhyo varo dvija
english: Viṣṇu said: I am pleased with your freedom from greed and your devotion, O best of twice-born ones. You must certainly receive a boon from me, O brahmin, O twice-born one.

sanskrit: evaṃ saṃchandyamānas tu vareṇa hariṇā tadā uttaṅkaḥ prāñjalir vavre varaṃ bharatasattama
english: Being thus urged to choose a boon by Hari, Uttaṅka then, with joined palms, requested a boon, O best of the Bhārata line.

sanskrit: yadi me bhagavān prītaḥ puṇḍarīkanibhekṣaṇaḥ dharme satye dame caiva buddhir bhavatu me sadā abhyāsaś ca bhaved bhaktyā tvayi nityaṃ maheśvara
english: "If you are pleased with me, O blessed one whose eyes resemble lotuses, may my mind ever abide in dharma, truth, and self-restraint; and may there be constant devotional practice toward you, O great lord."

sanskrit: viṣṇur uvāca sarvam etad dhi bhavitā matprasādāt tava dvija pratibhāsyati yogaś ca yena yukto divaukasām trayāṇām api lokānāṃ mahat kāryaṃ kariṣyasi
english: Viṣṇu said: All this shall indeed come to pass for you by my grace, O twice-born one. A yoga power shall be revealed to you by which, once yoked to it, you shall accomplish a great task for the three worlds of the celestials.

sanskrit: utsādanārthaṃ lokānāṃ dhundhur nāma mahāsuraḥ tapasyati tapo ghoraṃ śṛṇu yas taṃ haniṣyati
english: A great demon named Dhundhu is performing terrible austerities for the destruction of the worlds. Hear now who will slay him.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva iti khyāto bhaviṣyati mahīpatiḥ tasya putraḥ śucir dāntaḥ kuvalāśva iti śrutaḥ
english: A lord of the earth shall arise, known as Bṛhadaśva. His son, pure and self-controlled, is known as Kuvalāśva.

sanskrit: sa yogabalam āsthāya māmakaṃ pārthivottamaḥ śāsanāt tava viprarṣe dhundhumāro bhaviṣyati
english: That best of kings, relying on my yogic power and at your command, O sage among brahmins, shall become Dhundhumāra — the slayer of Dhundhu.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca uttaṅkam evam uktvā tu viṣṇur antaradhīyata
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Having thus spoken to Uttaṅka, Viṣṇu disappeared.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca ikṣvākau saṃsthite rājañ śaśādaḥ pṛthivīm imām prāptaḥ paramadharmātmā so 'yodhyāyāṃ nṛpo 'bhavat
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: When Ikṣvāku passed away, O king, Shasada obtained this earth — a man of supreme righteousness, he became king in Ayodhyā.

sanskrit: śaśādasya tu dāyādaḥ kakutstho nāma vīryavān anenāś cāpi kākutsthaḥ pṛthuś cānenasaḥ sutaḥ
english: Shasada's heir was the mighty Kākutstha. Kākutstha's son was Anenas, and Pṛthu was the son of Anenas.

sanskrit: viṣvagaśvaḥ pṛthoḥ putras tasmād ārdras tu jajñivān ārdrasya yuvanāśvas tu śrāvastas tasya cātmajaḥ
english: Vishvagashva was the son of Pṛthu; from him was born Ardra. Yuvanāśva was Ardra's son, and Shravasta was his own son.

sanskrit: jajñe śrāvastako rājā śrāvastī yena nirmitā śrāvastasya tu dāyādo bṛhadaśvo mahābalaḥ bṛhadaśvasutaś cāpi kuvalāśva iti smṛtaḥ
english: King Shravastaka was born, by whom the city of Shravasti was built. The heir of Shravasta was the greatly powerful Bṛhadaśva. Bṛhadaśva's son in turn is known as Kuvalāśva.

sanskrit: kuvalāśvasya putrāṇāṃ sahasrāṇy ekaviṃśatiḥ sarve vidyāsu niṣṇātā balavanto durāsadāḥ
english: Kuvalāśva had twenty-one thousand sons — all of them deeply versed in the sciences, powerful, and difficult to approach in battle.

sanskrit: kuvalāśvas tu pitṛto guṇair abhyadhiko 'bhavat samaye taṃ tato rājye bṛhadaśvo 'bhyaṣecayat kuvalāśvaṃ mahārāja śūram uttamadhārmikam
english: Kuvalāśva surpassed his father in virtues. In due time, therefore, Bṛhadaśva consecrated him to the kingdom, O great king — that heroic and supremely righteous Kuvalāśva.

sanskrit: putrasaṃkrāmitaśrīs tu bṛhadaśvo mahīpatiḥ jagāma tapase dhīmāṃs tapovanam amitrahā
english: Having transferred royal sovereignty to his son, the wise lord of the earth Bṛhadaśva, destroyer of foes, departed to a forest grove for ascetic practice.

sanskrit: atha śuśrāva rājarṣiṃ tam uttaṅko yudhiṣṭhira vanaṃ saṃprasthitaṃ rājan bṛhadaśvaṃ dvijottamaḥ
english: Then Uttaṅka the foremost of twice-born ones heard, O Yudhiṣṭhira, O king, that the royal sage Bṛhadaśva was setting forth to the forest.

sanskrit: tam uttaṅko mahātejāḥ sarvāstraviduṣāṃ varam nyavārayad ameyātmā samāsādya narottamam
english: The great-spirited Uttaṅka, of immense soul and vast splendor, met that best of men — the best of all who know weapons — and stopped him.

sanskrit: uttaṅka uvāca bhavatā rakṣaṇaṃ kāryaṃ tat tāvat kartum arhasi nirudvignā vayaṃ rājaṃs tvatprasādād vasemahi
english: Uttaṅka said: You must still perform the duty of protection. Please do so. By your grace, O king, may we dwell free from distress.

sanskrit: tvayā hi pṛthivī rājan rakṣyamāṇā mahātmanā bhaviṣyati nirudvignā nāraṇyaṃ gantum arhasi
english: For the earth, O king, protected by you, great-souled one, will be free from distress. You should not go to the forest.

sanskrit: pālane hi mahān dharmaḥ prajānām iha dṛśyate na tathā dṛśyate 'raṇye mā te bhūd buddhir īdṛśī
english: For great dharma is seen in the protection of subjects here in this world — it is not seen in that manner in the forest. Let not such a thought arise in you.

sanskrit: īdṛśo na hi rājendra dharmaḥ kva cana dṛśyate prajānāṃ pālane yo vai purā rājarṣibhiḥ kṛtaḥ rakṣitavyāḥ prajā rājñā tās tvaṃ rakṣitum arhasi
english: Such dharma as this — of protecting subjects, which was formerly practiced by royal sages — is not found anywhere else, O lord of kings. Subjects must be protected by the king; you should protect them.

sanskrit: nirudvignas tapaś cartuṃ na hi śaknomi pārthiva mamāśramasamīpe vai sameṣu marudhanvasu
english: For I am unable to practice austerities free from distress, O king, near my hermitage in the level sandy desert wastes.

sanskrit: samudro vālukāpūrṇa ujjānaka iti smṛtaḥ bahuyojanavistīrṇo bahuyojanam āyataḥ
english: There is a sea filled with sand, known as Ujjānaka — vast in extent across many yojanas and long across many yojanas.

sanskrit: tatra raudro dānavendro mahāvīryaparākramaḥ madhukaiṭabhayoḥ putro dhundhur nāma sudāruṇaḥ
english: There dwells a terrible lord of demons, of mighty valor and prowess — the son of Madhu and Kaiṭabha, known as Dhundhu — dreadfully fierce.

sanskrit: antarbhūmigato rājan vasaty amitavikramaḥ taṃ nihatya mahārāja vanaṃ tvaṃ gantum arhasi
english: He dwells inside the earth, O king, of immeasurable might. Having slain him, O great king, you may then go to the forest.

sanskrit: śete lokavināśāya tapa āsthāya dāruṇam tridaśānāṃ vināśāya lokānāṃ cāpi pārthiva
english: He lies in austerity, practicing terrible penance for the destruction of the worlds, for the ruin of the thirty gods and of the worlds, O king.

sanskrit: avadhyo devatānāṃ sa daityānām atha rakṣasām nāgānām atha yakṣāṇāṃ gandharvāṇāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ avāpya sa varaṃ rājan sarvalokapitāmahāt
english: He is invulnerable to gods, to Daityas, to Rākṣasas, to serpents, to Yakṣas, and to Gandharvas on every side, O king — having obtained a boon from the grandfather of all the worlds.

sanskrit: taṃ vināśaya bhadraṃ te mā te buddhir ato 'nyathā prāpsyase mahatīṃ kīrtiṃ śāśvatīm avyayāṃ dhruvām
english: Destroy him — good fortune to you! Let your mind not be otherwise. You shall attain great, eternal, imperishable, and enduring fame.

sanskrit: krūrasya svapatas tasya vālukāntarhitasya vai saṃvatsarasya paryante niḥśvāsaḥ saṃpravartate yadā tadā bhūś calati saśailavanakānanā
english: As that fierce one lies sleeping, hidden within the sand, at the end of each year his breath begins to move — and then the earth shakes along with its mountains, forests, and groves.

sanskrit: tasya niḥśvāsavātena raja uddhūyate mahat ādityapatham āvṛtya saptāhaṃ bhūmikampanam savisphuliṅgaṃ sajvālaṃ sadhūmaṃ hy atidāruṇam
english: By the wind of his breath, a great cloud of dust is hurled up, covering the path of the sun. For seven days the earth quakes, with sparks flying, with flames and smoke — most terrible.

sanskrit: tena rājan na śaknomi tasmin sthātuṃ sva āśrame taṃ vināśaya rājendra lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā lokāḥ svasthā bhavantv adya tasmin vinihate 'sure
english: Because of that, O king, I cannot remain in my own hermitage. Destroy him, O king of kings, out of desire for the welfare of the worlds. Let the worlds be at peace this day, once that demon is slain.

sanskrit: tvaṃ hi tasya vināśāya paryāpta iti me matiḥ tejasā tava tejaś ca viṣṇur āpyāyayiṣyati
english: You alone are capable of his destruction — this is my conviction. And Viṣṇu shall augment your splendor with his own splendor.

sanskrit: viṣṇunā ca varo datto mama pūrvaṃ tato vadhe yas taṃ mahāsuraṃ raudraṃ vadhiṣyati mahīpatiḥ tejas taṃ vaiṣṇavam iti pravekṣyati durāsadam
english: And a boon was given to me by Viṣṇu formerly in regard to his slaying: that the Vaiṣṇava splendor shall enter that lord of the earth who will slay that fierce and mighty demon, difficult to approach.

sanskrit: tat tejas tvaṃ samādhāya rājendra bhuvi duḥsaham taṃ niṣūdaya saṃduṣṭaṃ daityaṃ raudraparākramam
english: Absorbing that splendor — hard to bear on earth — O king of kings, slay that evil Daitya of fierce prowess.

sanskrit: na hi dhundhur mahātejās tejasālpena śakyate nirdagdhuṃ pṛthivīpāla sa hi varṣaśatair api
english: For the greatly splendid Dhundhu cannot be consumed with little splendor, O protector of the earth — not even in a hundred years.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca sa evam ukto rājarṣir uttaṅkenāparājitaḥ uttaṅkaṃ kauravaśreṣṭha kṛtāñjalir athābravīt
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: That royal sage, the unconquered one, thus addressed by Uttaṅka, then spoke to Uttaṅka with joined palms, O best of the Kauravas.

sanskrit: na te 'bhigamanaṃ brahman mogham etad bhaviṣyati putro mamāyaṃ bhagavan kuvalāśva iti smṛtaḥ
english: "Your coming to me, O brahmin, shall not be in vain. This son of mine, O blessed one, known as Kuvalāśva —

sanskrit: dhṛtimān kṣiprakārī ca vīryeṇāpratimo bhuvi priyaṃ vai sarvam etat te kariṣyati na saṃśayaḥ
english: "— steadfast and swift in action, unequaled in valor on earth — he shall surely do all that you desire. There is no doubt."

sanskrit: putraiḥ parivṛtaḥ sarvaiḥ śūraiḥ parighabāhubhiḥ visarjayasva māṃ brahman nyastaśastro 'smi sāṃpratam
english: "Send me forth, O brahmin, surrounded as I am by all my heroic sons with arms like iron clubs. I have now laid down my weapons."

sanskrit: tathāstv iti ca tenokto munināmitatejasā sa tam ādiśya tanayam uttaṅkāya mahātmane kriyatām iti rājarṣir jagāma vanam uttamam
english: Told "So be it" by the sage of immeasurable splendor, the royal sage directed his son to serve the great-souled Uttaṅka with the words "Let it be done," and departed to the excellent forest.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca ka eṣa bhagavan daityo mahāvīryas tapodhana kasya putro 'tha naptā vā etad icchāmi veditum
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Who is this demon, O blessed one, of great valor, O wealth of austerities? Whose son is he, or whose grandson? I wish to know this.

sanskrit: evaṃ mahābalo daityo na śruto me tapodhana etad icchāmi bhagavan yāthātathyena veditum sarvam eva mahāprājña vistareṇa tapodhana
english: Such a mighty demon — I have not heard of him, O wealth of austerities. I wish to know this fully in truth, O blessed one, O greatly wise one, O wealth of austerities, in detail.

sanskrit: mārkaṇḍeya uvāca śṛṇu rājann idaṃ sarvaṃ yathāvṛttaṃ narādhipa ekārṇave tadā ghore naṣṭe sthāvarajaṅgame pranaṣṭeṣu ca bhūteṣu sarveṣu bharatarṣabha
english: Mārkaṇḍeya said: Hear all this, O king, exactly as it occurred, O lord of men. At that time, in the terrible universal ocean, when stationary and moving things had perished, when all beings had disappeared, O bull of the Bhārata line —

sanskrit: prabhavaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ śāśvataḥ puruṣo 'vyayaḥ suṣvāpa bhagavān viṣṇur apśayyām eka eva ha nāgasya bhoge mahati śeṣasyāmitatejasaḥ
english: — the eternal, imperishable Person, the source of all beings, the blessed Viṣṇu slept alone upon a bed of water, on the great coils of the serpent Śeṣa of immeasurable splendor.

sanskrit: lokakartā mahābhāga bhagavān acyuto hariḥ nāgabhogena mahatā parirabhya mahīm imām
english: The blessed Acyuta Hari, maker of the worlds and greatly fortunate one, embraced this earth with the great coils of the serpent.

sanskrit: svapatas tasya devasya padmaṃ sūryasamaprabham nābhyāṃ viniḥsṛtaṃ tatra yatrotpannaḥ pitāmahaḥ sākṣāl lokagurur brahmā padme sūryendusaprabhe
english: From the navel of that sleeping god there issued forth a lotus brilliant as the sun, and therein was born the Grandfather himself — Brahmā, teacher of the worlds — on that lotus resplendent as sun and moon.

sanskrit: caturvedaś caturmūrtis tathaiva ca caturmukhaḥ svaprabhāvād durādharṣo mahābalaparākramaḥ
english: He of four Vedas, four forms, and likewise four faces — unapproachable through his own power, of great strength and valor.

sanskrit: kasya cit tv atha kālasya dānavau vīryavattarau madhuś ca kaiṭabhaś caiva dṛṣṭavantau hariṃ prabhum
english: Then after some time, two demons of exceeding valor — Madhu and Kaiṭabha — beheld Lord Hari.

sanskrit: śayānaṃ śayane divye nāgabhoge mahādyutim bahuyojanavistīrṇe bahuyojanam āyate
english: Lying on a divine couch, on the serpent's coils, greatly resplendent, extending across many yojanas in breadth and many yojanas in length.

sanskrit: kirīṭakaustubhadharaṃ pītakauśeyavāsasam dīpyamānaṃ śriyā rājaṃs tejasā vapuṣā tathā sahasrasūryapratimam adbhutopamadarśanam
english: Wearing a crown and the Kaustubha gem, clad in yellow silk garments, blazing with beauty, splendor, and form, O king — equal to a thousand suns, wonderful and beyond comparison to behold.

sanskrit: vismayaḥ sumahān āsīn madhukaiṭabhayos tadā dṛṣṭvā pitāmahaṃ caiva padme padmanibhekṣaṇam
english: There was great astonishment in Madhu and Kaiṭabha at that time, seeing also the Grandfather on the lotus, he whose eyes resemble lotuses.

sanskrit: vitrāsayetām atha tau brahmāṇam amitaujasam vitrāsyamāno bahuśo brahmā tābhyāṃ mahāyaśāḥ akampayat padmanālaṃ tato 'budhyata keśavaḥ
english: Then those two began to terrify Brahmā of immeasurable energy. As the greatly famous Brahmā was being terrified repeatedly by those two, he shook the lotus stalk — and thereby Keśava awakened.

sanskrit: athāpaśyata govindo dānavau vīryavattarau dṛṣṭvā tāv abravīd devaḥ svāgataṃ vāṃ mahābalau dadāni vāṃ varaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ prītir hi mama jāyate
english: Then Govinda saw the two demons of exceeding valor. Seeing those two, the god said: "Welcome to you both, O mighty ones. I shall grant you both a choice boon, for delight arises in me."

sanskrit: tau prahasya hṛṣīkeśaṃ mahāvīryau mahāsurau pratyabrūtāṃ mahārāja sahitau madhusūdanam
english: Those two great demons of mighty valor laughed and replied together to Hrishikesha, O great king — to Madhusūdana.

sanskrit: āvāṃ varaya deva tvaṃ varadau svaḥ surottama dātārau svo varaṃ tubhyaṃ tad bravīhy avicārayan
english: "You choose a boon from us, O god — we are boon-givers, O best of gods. We grant a boon to you — speak it without hesitation."

sanskrit: bhagavān uvāca pratigṛhṇe varaṃ vīrāv īpsitaś ca varo mama yuvāṃ hi vīryasaṃpannau na vām asti samaḥ pumān
english: The blessed one said: "I accept the boon, O heroes, and the desired boon from me is this: you two are endowed with valor — there is no man equal to you two.

sanskrit: vadhyatvam upagacchetāṃ mama satyaparākramau etad icchāmy ahaṃ kāmaṃ prāptuṃ lokahitāya vai
english: "Let you two, truly valorous, submit to being slain by me. This is the wish I desire to fulfill, for the welfare of the worlds."

sanskrit: madhukaiṭabhāv ūcatuḥ anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ nau svaireṣv api kuto 'nyathā satye dharme ca niratau viddhy āvāṃ puruṣottama
english: Madhu and Kaiṭabha said: "We have never spoken an untruth before — certainly not in casual matters; how then otherwise? Know us to be devoted to truth and dharma, O supreme Person.

sanskrit: bale rūpe ca vīrye ca śame ca na samo 'sti nau dharme tapasi dāne ca śīlasattvadameṣu ca
english: "In strength, beauty, valor, and equanimity — there is no one equal to us two; nor in dharma, austerity, giving, or in character, courage, and self-control.

sanskrit: upaplavo mahān asmān upāvartata keśava uktaṃ pratikuruṣva tvaṃ kālo hi duratikramaḥ
english: "A great flood is approaching us, O Keśava. Fulfill what was spoken — for time is difficult to transgress.

sanskrit: āvām icchāvahe deva kṛtam ekaṃ tvayā vibho anāvṛte 'sminn ākāśe vadhaṃ suravarottama
english: "We desire this of you, O god — let one thing be done by you, O lord: let our slaying take place in this unobstructed open sky, O best among the gods."
